blurb: Stocky British mastiff-type dog with a broad head, loose skin folds and an underbite
description: The Bulldog is a medium-sized British breed of mastiff type with a large head, flat face and short coat, described as friendly and courageous.
answer: The Bulldog, also called the English or British Bulldog, is a British breed of mastiff type developed as a companion from the extinct Old English Bulldog. It is stocky and muscular, with a large head, thick facial folds and a flat face with a protruding lower jaw, and is generally described as friendly and amiable.

body: Its ancestors were used for bull-baiting until the sport was outlawed in England in 1835, after which the breed was kept as a companion. The Bulldog Club founded in 1875 is described as the oldest single-breed club in the world, and the American Kennel Club recognised the breed in 1886. After health concerns were publicised, the Kennel Club revised the standard in 2009, and the Netherlands restricts breeding of dogs with very short snouts, including Bulldogs.

Bulldogs have wide heads and shoulders, a pronounced underbite, folds of skin on the brow, a nose roll above the short muzzle and hanging skin under the neck. The coat is short, flat and sleek in red, fawn, white, brindle and piebald. Dogs weigh about 25 kg and bitches about 23 kg, with lower standard weights in the United States.

The American Kennel Club standard calls for an equable, kind, resolute and courageous disposition that is not vicious or aggressive. Bulldogs are known for getting along well with children, other dogs and other pets.

The modern Bulldog is described as not suited to significant physical exertion. Because the flat face makes it hard to cool down by panting, it is prone to overheating, and many airlines will not carry the breed in the cargo hold.

A Royal Veterinary College study found Bulldogs had over twice the odds of being diagnosed with at least one common disorder. Conditions reported in the breed include brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome, hip dysplasia, patellar luxation, skin fold and atopic dermatitis, demodicosis and hiatal hernia. Over 80% of litters are delivered by Caesarean section. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 9.8 years.

faq.q: How big does a Bulldog get?
faq.a: Bulldogs are medium-sized; standards give about 25 kg for males and 23 kg for females, with lower weights in the United States.
Bulldogs are known for getting along well with children, other dogs and other pets.
A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 9.8 years, and a 2022 UK study found 7.39 years.

faq.q: Is the Bulldog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists the Bulldog as breed number 149 in Group 2.
